To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the shear-mode crack growth is influenced by the crystal lattice and the presence of the second-phase particles.
the presence of secondary phases and their crystallographic orientation are the key factors in determining the effective mode II threshold and the crack path.
the effective resistance to shear-mode crack growth depends on the microstructure, the crystal lattice type (ferritic or pearlitic) and the stacking fault energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the crystallographic structure and the secondary-phase particles on the effective resistance to shear-mode cracks.
the effective resistance of the ferritic- pearlitic and pearlite steels to shear-mode fatigue cracks.
the influence of crystal structure and microstructure on the effective resistance to mode II and mode I crack growth in steels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effective threshold is the most important factor for the shear-mode fatigue growth, while the microstructure and crystal structure play a secondary role.

in the ferritic and pearlitic microstructures the shear mode I cracks were deflected to mode I due to the presence of the cementite particles and that the mode I cracks were not deflected by a high stacking fault energy.
the effective mode II threshold is a good parameter for the prediction of the shear-mode fatigue behaviour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of a secondary phase, such as cementite in the steel, can be considered as a main factor that influences the effective resistance of a material against shear-mode crack growth.
the effective mode II thresholds are a useful parameter for the evaluation of the shear mode fatigue crack growth resistance of the material.

the effective resistance and near-threshold growth behaviour of the shear-mode fatigue cracks are controlled by the microstructure and crystal lattice type, and that these two factors are not independent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the ferritic steel with the presence of the pearlite, the mode I crack-tip stress state is much more important for crack propagation than the local mode II.
the shear-mode fatigue cracks can be effectively deflected by the presence of the second-phase particles in the ferritic steel.
, when the material is subjected to the mode II loading, the effective mode I resistance should be taken into account, as the crack can deflect from the mode II to the mode I loading.
